name: edge-tts

findings.evidence: When no whitespace appears within the first 4096 bytes, _find_safe_utf8_split_point receives all remaining text rather than text[:byte_length]. It returns the whole valid UTF-8 string. 10,000 unspaced ASCII bytes produce [10000]; 3,000 Han characters produce [9000].
findings.impact: Long text without spaces is not bounded per request. CJK passages, long tokens and URLs can create arbitrarily large SSML/WebSocket requests instead of being segmented, exposing synthesis to service request-size limits.
findings.recommendation: Pass text[:byte_length] into the UTF-8 boundary finder, reject a zero split point when one complete character/entity cannot fit, and preserve all content across chunks.
findings.validation: Confirmed using actual split_text_by_byte_length through /workspace/review/edge_repros.py. Remote service rejection not exercised.
findings.title: Unspaced text bypasses the 4096-byte chunk limit

findings.evidence: The worker enqueues its sentinel only after a clean async iteration; executor.submit's Future is discarded. If stream raises, no sentinel or error enters the queue and the consumer blocks indefinitely on queue.get().
findings.impact: A network/transport/synthesis exception makes the public stream_sync caller hang permanently instead of receiving the original failure.
findings.recommendation: Always communicate completion from a finally block, transfer the worker exception to the consumer, close the event loop in finally, and retain/check the Future.
findings.validation: Subclassed actual Communicate with an async stream that raises RuntimeError; next(stream_sync()) hung until a subprocess timeout killed it after 2 seconds. Reproduction saved in /workspace/review/edge_repros.py.
findings.title: Synchronous streaming hangs after worker errors

findings.evidence: Every text chunk creates ClientSession(connector=self.connector) with aiohttp's default connector_owner=True. Exiting the first chunk session closes the caller-supplied connector. The next chunk reuses that closed connector.
findings.impact: Any multi-chunk synthesis using the supported custom connector argument fails on its second chunk with RuntimeError('Session is closed'); a 403 retry can also reuse the closed connector.
findings.recommendation: Use one session for the complete stream/retry lifetime, or set connector_owner=False for supplied connectors while retaining ownership for internally created connectors.
findings.validation: Actual Communicate.stream against a loopback aiohttp WebSocket fixture delivered the first chunk, closed the custom TCPConnector, then raised 'Session is closed' before opening a second request. Saved in /workspace/review/edge_repros.py.
findings.title: Multi-chunk synthesis closes the caller-supplied connector

architecture.product: Python library and CLI for Microsoft's online Edge text-to-speech service, with optional audio playback and subtitle output.
runtime_flow: Communicate.__init__ validates voice/prosody, sanitizes text, XML-escapes it and creates a lazy byte-chunk generator.
Communicate.stream iterates text chunks, invokes a per-chunk WebSocket exchange and retries once after supported HTTP 403 clock-skew handling.
Communicate.__stream sends configuration plus generated SSML, then yields MP3 audio and boundary metadata; chunk audio byte counts adjust subsequent timing offsets.
save writes streamed audio and metadata; stream_sync bridges the async generator through a worker thread and Queue; save_sync runs async save through a worker Future.
CLI/util modules compose library synthesis with subtitles; edge_playback modules use OS/player integration.

contracts_to_preserve: Communicate.stream is single-use and yields the existing audio and boundary-metadata shapes.

setup.cfg declares Python >=3.7; use syntax and standard-library APIs compatible with the supported interpreter range, or separately approve a support-range change.

immediate_mitigations.action: Reject or divide very long user input at safe natural boundaries before synthesis, keeping each original input short enough that XML escaping cannot exceed the intended chunk cap.
immediate_mitigations.limit: This caller-side workaround requires UTF-8/escaping-aware sizing and does not repair the library's no-whitespace fallback. Actual Microsoft request-size rejection was not exercised.

immediate_mitigations.action: Use async for over Communicate.stream() with normal exception handling for applications that can use asyncio. If the sync API must be isolated before repair, enforce a timeout from a process boundary that can terminate the blocked worker.
immediate_mitigations.limit: A timeout on the same consumer thread does not unblock Queue.get(). This workaround does not add cancellation or exception propagation to stream_sync.

immediate_mitigations.action: Omit the optional connector argument where a custom connector is unnecessary, allowing a new internally owned connector per chunk.
immediate_mitigations.limit: Applications requiring custom DNS, routing, TLS or connection policy still need the ownership fix. Do not weaken TLS or routing controls to adopt this workaround.

findings.title: No-whitespace fallback emits an unbounded text chunk
findings.evidence: _find_safe_utf8_split_point(text) scans the entire remaining text rather than the first byte_length bytes. A valid 10,000-byte unspaced ASCII string yields [10000]; 3,000 Han characters yield [9000], although byte_length=4096.
findings.user_impact: Long CJK passages or unbroken tokens can become arbitrarily large SSML/WebSocket requests. The local evidence proves the cap violation; it does not prove how the remote service handles every oversized request.
change_surface: Focused regression tests to be added; no current unit-test target exists
concrete_repair_steps: Give the UTF-8 fallback only the bounded prefix text[:byte_length], leaving the remainder for subsequent iterations.
After entity adjustment, detect the no-progress case explicitly. Raise the documented ValueError when a complete leading character/entity cannot fit rather than dropping one content byte.
Preserve whitespace preference and existing chunk stripping; avoid introducing Unicode decode/encode cycles that change original content.
Add direct chunk-property tests, then exercise Communicate.texts so the sanitation/escaping path is covered.
invariants: Every nonempty emitted chunk has len(chunk) <= byte_length.
Each chunk independently decodes as UTF-8.
An XML entity is never split between chunks.
Non-whitespace content is neither lost nor duplicated; no-whitespace test inputs reconstruct byte-for-byte.
Every iteration consumes input or raises a documented error.
acceptance_criteria: 10,000 unspaced ASCII bytes are split into bounded chunks whose concatenation equals the input.
3,000 Han characters split at valid UTF-8 boundaries, with each chunk <=4096 bytes and complete reconstruction.
Escaped ampersands and angle brackets around the limit produce valid entity boundaries.
A positive limit too small for the next complete character/entity raises ValueError promptly without data loss or an infinite loop.
Whitespace-rich baseline inputs continue using the established natural-boundary behavior.
regression_scenarios: Exactly 4096 ASCII bytes; 4097 bytes; a 4-byte Unicode character crossing a byte boundary.
CJK text with no spaces; a very long URL/token.
XML entities whose final semicolon lies just beyond the proposed split.
Empty text, bytes input, nonpositive byte_length and invalid input type.
risks: Fixing the fallback increases the number of requests for previously unbounded text and can expose the separate connector-lifetime defect unless EDGE-3 is repaired.
Incorrect zero-progress handling can silently drop a character or the opening ampersand of an entity.
Chunk-boundary timing/subtitles need combined validation because more service turns are generated.
findings.rollback: Revert the isolated splitter repair if an unexpected regression occurs, restore caller-side long-input limits, and leave the defect recorded as OPEN. Reverting reintroduces oversized requests.

findings.title: Synchronous streaming hangs when the async producer fails
findings.evidence: The worker puts its None sentinel only after successful async iteration. The submitted Future is discarded. A worker exception leaves the consumer blocked forever in queue.get(). A synthetic RuntimeError hung until a 2-second subprocess timeout killed it.
findings.user_impact: A transport or synthesis failure can permanently block the application's synchronous caller instead of surfacing the cause.
change_surface: New focused offline sync-bridge regression tests
concrete_repair_steps: Retain the Future returned by executor.submit.
Ensure the worker signals terminal completion from an outer finally block covering event-loop creation/execution as well as async iteration.
After receiving terminal completion, consume future.result() or an explicit queued error so the original failure is raised in the caller; do not translate failure into normal end-of-stream.
Close the worker event loop in finally on both success and failure.
If early consumer close/cancellation is changed, implement and verify that ownership separately; do not introduce a bounded-queue shutdown deadlock.
invariants: Each producer exit wakes the consumer exactly once.
The caller receives the original worker exception after any already-yielded items.
Success preserves item order and clean iteration termination.
The event loop and executor thread are cleaned up after failure.
No queued audio or metadata is silently discarded by an ambiguous sentinel.
acceptance_criteria: A producer that raises before its first item causes next(stream_sync()) to raise the same failure promptly instead of timing out.
A producer that yields one item and then raises delivers that item followed by the failure.
A successful empty or multi-item producer terminates normally with order preserved.
Repeated failures do not accumulate worker threads or event-loop resource warnings.
Any intended behavior for an early-closed synchronous iterator is documented and locally checked.
regression_scenarios: Failure before first yield, between audio chunks, and after metadata.
RuntimeError and a representative aiohttp transport exception.
Successful empty and normal multi-item streams.
Repeated independent synchronous calls after previous failures.
Consumer closes the generator early; verify no new deadlock is introduced.
risks: A sentinel-only repair can incorrectly turn an error into successful EOF unless the Future or error payload is inspected.
Handling only Exception in the wrong scope can still miss producer exit before iteration starts.
Introducing queue backpressure without coordinated cancellation can block executor shutdown.
findings.rollback: Revert this isolated sync bridge change if it alters success behavior unexpectedly. Prefer the async API or an external process timeout while the defect remains open; the previous sync behavior still hangs on errors.

findings.title: The first chunk closes the custom connector needed by later chunks
findings.evidence: Every __stream invocation constructs aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=self.connector) with default connector_owner=True. The local fixture completes the first chunk and closes the supplied TCPConnector; the second chunk fails with RuntimeError('Session is closed') before a second WebSocket request opens.
findings.user_impact: Multi-chunk synthesis with the supported connector parameter fails after the first chunk. A retry can encounter the same closed-connector problem.
change_surface: Communicate.stream chunk/retry lifetime if choosing one shared session
concrete_repair_steps: Choose one minimal ownership model: retain per-chunk sessions and set connector_owner=False only for a caller-supplied connector, or move a single session around the whole stream/retry lifetime.
Keep internally created connectors owned and closed by their session.
Document that the caller closes a supplied connector when all dependent work is finished.
Preserve timeout, trust_env, proxy, TLS context and HTTP 403 retry behavior.
Exercise both the multi-chunk path and retry behavior with a local fixture.
findings.preferred_approach: Set connector_owner=False when self.connector is supplied; this is the smaller repair surface. A whole-stream session is a viable alternative if its cleanup, retry and timing effects are tested.
invariants: Caller-supplied connectors remain open after the stream unless the caller closes them.
Internally allocated connectors are released on clean completion and exceptions.
Every required chunk can establish its WebSocket exchange.
A supported 403 retry can reuse the intended connector.
Session ownership changes do not disable TLS or bypass proxy policy.
acceptance_criteria: The existing 5,000-character whitespace-rich input against the local fixture opens at least two requests and completes without 'Session is closed'.
A supplied connector remains open until the test caller closes it.
The default connector path succeeds across multiple chunks without resource warnings.
A forced supported 403 retry does not fail due to premature connector closure.
Exception and cancellation paths leave no internally owned connector/session leak.
regression_scenarios: Single versus multiple chunks, with and without a supplied connector.
Two independent Communicate objects sharing one caller-owned connector.
First-attempt 403 followed by success; unretryable HTTP failure.
Failure after first audio bytes and early iteration termination.
Custom connector plus explicit proxy/timeout settings.
risks: Setting connector_owner=False unconditionally would leak internally created connectors.
Changing the whole-stream session scope can alter connection pooling and error cleanup.
Applications that accidentally relied on the library closing a supplied connector need the ownership behavior documented.
findings.rollback: Revert the isolated ownership repair if necessary and omit custom connectors where their policy is unnecessary. Reverting preserves the known failure for long input with supplied connectors.
